title: Completed inverse image of an integral line with a slice basis
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a scheme X on which l is invertible. Let W be an object of the small pro-etale site of X. Put R_X equal to the completed integral coefficient sheaf, and R_W to the corresponding sheaf on W.left [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For a rank-one locally free R_X-module sheaf L and an isomorphism from its restriction to the slice at W to the regular coefficient module restricted to that slice, the actual completed derived inverse image [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] along W.hom of L placed in degree zero is isomorphic to R_W placed in degree zero. No noetherian or dimension hypothesis on X is imposed.

Proof (3), local triviality of integral, rational and algebraically closed coefficient lines

proof.text: Place L in degree zero. A locally free line is flat, so this is a flat-term K-flat representative for the actual integral completed pullback. Use the representative comparison from integralOperationsWellDefined to express the result as Q of the strict Roos complex of finite quotient inverse images.

At exponent n+1, extend the given slice basis to the finite coefficient quotient. Object inverse image is restriction to the slice followed by the pro-etale slice equivalence, and its constant-ring normalization sends the regular coefficient module to the regular coefficient module. Thus each finite pulled-back term is the regular quotient module. All bases are reductions of the same integral basis; hence the maps commute with every quotient transition and augmentation, not merely separately in the derived categories.

Apply products and the signed mapping-cocone functor to this strict tower isomorphism. The regular completed coefficient module is derived complete and its locally surjective quotient tower has the coefficient ring as limit. Its normalized augmentation to the quotient-tower Roos complex is a quasi-isomorphism. Compose this augmentation inverse with the representative and strict-tower comparisons to obtain the displayed isomorphism.

theorem integralObjectPullbackLine (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)] (W : X.ProEt)
    (L : integralTowerModules l E X) (hL : L.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1)
    (e : L.over W ≅
      (SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E X)).over W) :
    Nonempty ((integralDerivedPullback l E W.hom).obj
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E W.left)))
